Gladys integration for **Tailwind** garage door controllers (iQ3, Light), on
your local network: the state of each garage door, Open and Close buttons, and
the brightness of the status LED, through the local API of the controller,
without the Tailwind cloud.

> **Never tested with a real device.** This first version was built from the
> `gotailwind` library (the one of the Home Assistant integration) and tested
> against simulated controllers only. Feedback welcome.
>
> Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Tailwind.

## What you need

- A Tailwind controller with firmware **10.10 or later** (update it in the
  Tailwind app), on the same network as Gladys.
- A **fixed IP address** for each controller (a DHCP reservation in your
  router).
- Your **local control key**: sign in to the Tailwind web app
  (web.gotailwind.com) with your Tailwind account, and copy the six-digit
  "Local Control Key". It is the same for every controller of the account.
  Gladys never talks to the Tailwind cloud: you only read the key there.

## Setup

1. In Gladys, open the integration configuration.
2. Type the IP addresses of your controllers, separated by commas.
3. Paste the local control key. This field is kept by Gladys in its database,
   never shown again, and sent only to your controllers, in clear on your
   local network (their local API has no https).
4. Save, then add the controllers from the **Discovery** tab.

The status line says how many controllers answer. **Check the controllers**
shows what each address answered.

## What you get

One Gladys device per controller (identified by its MAC address: a new IP
address changes nothing), with for each door it manages (1 to 3):

| Feature               | Type           | Notes                                          |
| --------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Garage door _n_       | opening sensor | open or closed; nothing published when unknown |
| Open garage door _n_  | button         | refused until allowed (see below)              |
| Close garage door _n_ | button         | refused until allowed (see below)              |

and **Status LED brightness** (0 to 100), which needs no permission. A
brightness change is confirmed only when the LED is read back at the value
asked; otherwise Gladys answers "sent, without confirmation".

## Command safety

A Tailwind controller opens and closes a door by pulsing the wall-button input
of the opener. On most openers that input is a **toggle**: a pulse given to a
door that moved since it was read can stop or reverse it. So:

- **Open** and **Close** are both **refused by default**. Turn on "Allow
  opening and closing the garage doors" to use them (from the dashboard, the
  scenes and the voice assistants alike). The permission is checked when the
  command arrives, after the door is read and right before the request leaves.
- The door is never a switch: a "turn everything off" from a voice assistant
  or a scene can never reach it.
- Gladys reads the controller just before each command and checks that it is
  the same controller (MAC). **Open** is sent only to a door read closed,
  **Close** only to a door read open; already there: nothing is sent. A door
  in an unknown state, disabled in the Tailwind app or locked out by the
  controller is refused.
- After a command, the next one of that door waits until the door is read
  where it was sent: at least **30 s after an opening** (the sensor reads
  "open" as soon as the door leaves closed, long before the end of a travel
  of up to 30 s), 15 s after a closing ("closed" is only read at the end of
  travel), 45 s at most. This guard is written to the integration files
  before the request leaves, so a restart keeps it, and it is timed on a
  clock that a change of the system time does not move.
- A **Close** never waits behind another command, of its door or of another
  door: closing three doors at once sends three commands. It cancels the
  openings of its door that have not left yet. It is never held by a pause
  asked by the controller (HTTP 429 or 5xx) nor by a refused key: it gets one
  try, never retried. Openings of a same door go one at a time.
- **Open** pressed again on the same door within 5 s of an opening that sent
  nothing (door read open, or refused) is refused without reading the
  controller again ("try again in a few seconds"): a scene in a loop never
  floods it. **Close** is never held this way: every close reads the door
  again and decides on what it reads. The LED brightness can change once
  every 2 s at most.
- If the integration cannot write to its files, a command still leaves (its
  guard holds in memory) and the status says so.
- A command leaves within 3.5 s of the click or is refused without sending
  anything. If it may have reached the controller without an answer, Gladys
  says "sent, without confirmation" and reads the door again; it is never
  retried. A successful answer means the controller accepted the command: the
  door then moves for 10 to 30 s and its state follows in Gladys.

## Limits

- Polling only (every 10 s by default, 5 s to 300 s), never sooner than the
  interval, even after a restart. HTTP 429 or 5xx: a pause of 1 min to 6 h.
- A key refused by a controller is final for that controller: it is not read
  again with that key until you save another key, or press "Check the
  controllers" once the key is fixed (one read, never sooner than the
  interval). The key is never written in the logs nor in the integration
  files: only 8 bits of a salted fingerprint of a refused key are kept (the
  key cannot be found back from them), removed at the first success. An entry
  of the addresses field that is not an address is never shown in the
  status, only counted.
- The night mode, the notifications pushed by the controller and the mDNS
  discovery are not handled yet.
- Most Tailwind controllers are sold in North America: the integration may
  be of little use elsewhere.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Tailwind in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Tailwind controllers, on your local network | `section` | Nein | The state of each garage door of your Tailwind controllers (iQ3, Light), Open and Close buttons, and the brightness of the status LED, through the local API of the controller, without the Tailwind cloud. Give each controller a fixed IP address in your router, type the addresses and your local control key below, then add them from the Discovery tab. Never tested with a real device. Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Tailwind. |
| IP addresses of the controllers | `string` | Nein | Separated by commas, for example 192.168.1.60, 192.168.1.61 (add :port if it is not 80). |
| Local control key | `secret` | Nein | The six-digit "Local Control Key" shown in the Tailwind web app (web.gotailwind.com, signed in with your Tailwind account). The same for every controller of the account. Needed for everything: a controller answers nothing without it. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to your Tailwind controllers (in clear on your local network: their local API has no https). |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | Nein | How often each controller is read, in seconds. Never sooner, even after a restart. |
| Opening and closing | `section` | Nein | Each door has two buttons, never a switch. The controller pulses the wall-button input of the opener, a toggle on most openers: a pulse can stop or reverse a door that moved since it was read. Both buttons are therefore refused until you allow them below. Gladys reads the door just before each command: "Open" only to a door read closed, "Close" only to a door read open; unknown, disabled or locked out: refused. After a command, the next one of that door waits until it is read where it was sent: at least 30 s after an opening (a door is read open as soon as it leaves closed), 15 s after a closing, 45 s at most. A close never waits behind another command and is never held by a pause asked by the controller. Without the permission, a scene or a voice assistant "close the garage" is refused too. |
| Allow opening and closing the garage doors | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default: the doors are only read. On: the dashboard, the scenes and the voice assistants can open AND close the garage doors. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | Nein | Used for the names of the features added from now on, and for the command errors. |

## So installierst du Tailwind in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Tailwind erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-tailwind:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-tailwind](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-tailwind).

Tailwind benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Tailwind ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
